title: H-RIVALPARITY-1 part A (user-approved 2026-09-27): per-player rival attention - solo host = native only; the host's per-key count for Client1 equals the client's own GetPlayerValues; Client1's intro + activation happen for Client1 only (text to Client1, host state unchanged); save/reload keeps the store; rivaltimeline report
preconditions: Fixture save1 (host melaus, client Client1; 4 rivals, Murray Hill special rival ju1yVbREcE2B5ymg6q5tyA==). Its manifest predates RivalAttention = the MIGRATION path (clients start fresh). Build H-RIVALPARITY-1 A deployed on both machines. Writes ONE scratch slot (the -auto rotation sibling); the fixture's own save1 is never overwritten.
oracles_absent: \[RivalAttn\] (sweep|tick|step|check|count|snapshot|settle load|host rows|manifest restore|set active|sweep postfix|merged host count|text)[^\]]*:

steps.note: the host's world loads; NO client yet - the SOLO-HOST phase (test 4)

steps.expect_result: ^OK rivalattn host hostKey=p:\S+ keys=0 firings=0 sig=\S+ rivals=\[[^;]*\]$
steps.note: TEST 4: only the host key (no ';' = no second key row on any rival), no mod-path firing
the game's own hourly sweep, run now: the native path, then the postfix (which must do nothing solo)
longer than the 10-30 s native delay: any mod-path step would have run

steps.expect_result: ^OK rivalattn host hostKey=${hostKey} keys=0 firings=0 sig=\S+ rivals=\[[^;]*\]$
steps.note: TEST 4 after a sweep: still the host key only, 0 firings
REPORT: the Murray Hill rival's allEntries (copycat / overlapping price entries decide the manager's gate question)
the host's own (native) Murray Hill state before any client
a later joiner parks for the host's approval popup; the lever accepts it
the client is served its save and settles
the self-report now (else up to 120 s old)

steps.expect_result: ^OK rivalattn local pid=${clientPid} rivals=\[ju1yVbREcE2B5ymg6q5tyA==\{[^}]*\}: native count=(\d+) income=-?\d+ reported=\1 active=0
steps.note: TEST 1 (client side): the game's own GetPlayerValues ON the client; reported = the self-report's RivalQualifying rows (must agree); active=0 = CLIENTS START FRESH (per-peer R3)
TEST 1 (host side): the host's per-key count for Client1 equals the client's native count
REPORT: the same timeline data on the client
DEV floor: Client1's count reads at least 3 on this rival (the fixture's real Murray Hill count is reported in the COUNT block)

expect_log.regex: \[RivalAttn\] intro '[^']+' for p:\S+ on ju1yVbREcE2B5ymg6q5tyA==: text to 1 player\(s\) \[${clientPid}\]

steps.note: TEST 2a: Client1's intro, 10-30 s after the check, as TEXT to Client1 only

expect_log.regex: \[RivalAttn\] ACTIVATED rival ju1yVbREcE2B5ymg6q5tyA== for p:\S+ \(special text to 1 player

steps.note: TEST 2b: the next check activates the rival for Client1 (intro already sent), after the native delay
the per-peer heartbeat publish (3 s)
TEST 2: active on Client1's machine
TEST 2: the host's own Murray Hill state is unchanged
the per-peer signature the host expects on Client1

Client1 holds its own key's state for the rival: the host's active / defeated / defense part exactly, and AT LEAST the key's sent keys (entrance + activation). Part D F1 (2026-09-27) made the client's apply ADD-ONLY, so keys the client recorded itself (or its served save already held) stay - an exact whole-signature match no longer holds by design
TEST 3: the store signature before the save
the client's upload reaches the host and the slot manifest is stamped
an in-game client served a reload exits to the menu (T-WALLETDUPE pattern): the member leaves, the host loads, the member comes back
the host's world loads
TEST 3: identical after the reload (taken BEFORE Client1 is back, so no check can move it)
the member returns
the DEV floor is memory-only; re-applied so the next natural check does not deactivate on the real count
the per-peer JOIN snapshot carries Client1's own restored state
the host's own Murray Hill state survived the reload unchanged
